hints: At constant speed on a level road, driving force equals the sum of resistances: $F_D = 650 + 150 = 800\text{ N}$.
Use $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Multiply $800 \times 24$ to find the power in watts, and divide by $1000$ for kW.
walkthrough:
Identify the equilibrium of horizontal forces for steady motion at $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
Because the car and caravan move at constant speed, their acceleration is zero ($a = 0$).
By Newton's first law, the forward driving force $F_D$ must balance total resistive forces:
$$F_D = R_{\text{car}} + R_{\text{caravan}} = 650 + 150 = 800\text{ N}$$

Apply the power-force-velocity relation:
$$P = F_D \times v$$
Substitute $F_D = 800\text{ N}$ and $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 800 \times 24$$
$$800 \times 24 = 19\,200\text{ W}$$
Converting to kilowatts:
$$P = \frac{19\,200}{1000} = 19.2\text{ kW}$$
Thus, the power of the car's engine is $19\,200\text{ W}$ (or $19.2\text{ kW}$).

hints: Calculate the new driving force at $40\text{ kW}$ and speed $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F_D = \frac{40\,000}{24} = \frac{5000}{3}\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law to the entire system: $F_D - 800 = (1750 + 500)a$, and solve for acceleration $a$.
Apply Newton's second law to the caravan alone: $T - 150 = 500a$, and substitute $a$ to find tow-bar tension $T$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the new forward driving force immediately after power increases to $40\text{ kW} = 40\,000\text{ W}$:
At the instant of the power increase, the speed is still $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{40\,000}{24} = \frac{5000}{3}\text{ N} \approx 1666.67\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the combined car-caravan system:
- Total mass: $M = 1750 + 500 = 2250\text{ kg}$
- Total resistance: $R_{\text{total}} = 650 + 150 = 800\text{ N}$
$$\sum F = M a$$
$$F_D - R_{\text{total}} = M a$$
$$\frac{5000}{3} - 800 = 2250a$$
$$\frac{5000 - 2400}{3} = 2250a$$
$$\frac{2600}{3} = 2250a$$
Divide both sides by $2250$:
$$a = \frac{2600}{3 \times 2250} = \frac{2600}{6750} = \frac{52}{135} \approx 0.38518\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $a = 0.385\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Isolate the caravan to find the tension $T$ in the tow-bar:
Forces acting on the caravan of mass $m = 500\text{ kg}$:
- Forward pull from tow-bar: $T$
- Backward resistance: $R_{\text{caravan}} = 150\text{ N}$
$$\sum F = m a$$
$$T - 150 = 500a$$
$$T = 150 + 500\left(\frac{52}{135}\right)$$
Simplify the fraction:
$$\frac{500 \times 52}{135} = \frac{100 \times 52}{27} = \frac{5200}{27}$$
$$T = 150 + \frac{5200}{27} = \frac{150 \times 27 + 5200}{27} = \frac{4050 + 5200}{27} = \frac{9250}{27}\text{ N}$$
Compute the decimal equivalent:
$$T = 342.59\ldots \approx 343\text{ N}$$
Thus, the instantaneous acceleration is $0.385\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and the tension in the tow-bar is $343\text{ N}$.

hints: Calculate the total downhill opposing force: sum of resistances ($650 + 150 = 800\text{ N}$) plus total downhill weight $(1750 + 500)g\sin\theta$.
Substitute $M = 2250\text{ kg}$ and $\sin\theta = 0.14$ to find total resisting force: $800 + 2250(10)(0.14) = 3950\text{ N}$.
Equate driving force to $\frac{P}{v}$ with $P = 31\,000\text{ W}$ and solve $\frac{31\,000}{v} = 3950$ for $v$.
walkthrough:
Identify all forces opposing the car-caravan system along the inclined hill:
- Mass of car: $1750\text{ kg}$, resistance: $650\text{ N}$
- Mass of caravan: $500\text{ kg}$, resistance: $150\text{ N}$
- Total mass: $M = 1750 + 500 = 2250\text{ kg}$
- Incline angle: $\sin\theta = 0.14$
- Total non-gravitational resistance: $R_{\text{total}} = 650 + 150 = 800\text{ N}$

Calculate the downhill component of gravitational force:
$$W_{\parallel} = Mg\sin\theta = (2250)(10)(0.14) = 22\,500 \times 0.14 = 3150\text{ N}$$

Calculate the required driving force at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$\sum F_{\parallel} = 0$$
$$F_D - R_{\text{total}} - W_{\parallel} = 0$$
$$F_D = 800 + 3150 = 3950\text{ N}$$

Relate driving force to engine power output:
$$P = 31\text{ kW} = 31\,000\text{ W}$$
$$P = F_D \times v$$
$$31\,000 = 3950 \times v$$

Solve for the steady speed $v$:
$$v = \frac{31\,000}{3950} = \frac{3100}{395} = \frac{620}{79}$$
Compute the decimal equivalent:
$$\frac{620}{79} \approx 7.8481\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $v = 7.85\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
